Name: Ollama
Cost: Free software; models use Pi disk/RAM/CPU. No API bill unless connected to outside services.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Install dependencies, download/install Ollama for Linux/ARM if supported, run 'ollama serve', then pull a small model such as 'ollama pull llama3.2:1b'. Best on Raspberry Pi 5 or stronger.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'sudo systemctl disable --now ollama' if installed as a service. Remove the Ollama binary/service files and delete model storage if you want the models gone.

Name: llama.cpp
Cost: Free open-source software; you provide/download GGUF models. No web bill.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Run: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git cmake build-essential. Then: git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp && cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j$(nproc). Download a small GGUF model separately.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Stop any service you created. Delete the source folder with 'rm -rf ~/llama.cpp'. Delete downloaded model files from wherever you stored them.

Name: llamafile
Cost: Free open-source software; you download one executable model file. No web bill.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Download a .llamafile, run 'chmod +x model.llamafile', then start it with './model.llamafile'. This is useful when you want one file that runs the model.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Stop the running process. Delete the .llamafile with 'rm model.llamafile'. Remove any systemd service file if you created one.

Name: LocalAI
Cost: Free open-source software; can be resource-heavy. No API bill unless bridged to paid services.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Install Docker, then run LocalAI as a Docker container. Put models/config files in a persistent folder. Useful when you want an OpenAI-compatible local API.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'docker stop localai' and 'docker rm localai'. Remove the image if desired. Delete the model/config folder. Remove Docker only if you installed Docker just for LocalAI.

Name: OpenAI API
Cost: Paid per API usage; pricing depends on model and tool usage.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Create a Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv ~/aiweb && source ~/aiweb/bin/activate && pip install openai. Store the key as OPENAI_API_KEY. Your Pi script calls the web API instead of running the model locally.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'pip uninstall openai'. Delete ~/aiweb if unused. Remove OPENAI_API_KEY from .bashrc, .profile, .env, or systemd service files.

Name: Google Gemini API
Cost: Free developer tier may be available with limits; paid tiers for higher use.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Create a Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv ~/aiweb && source ~/aiweb/bin/activate && pip install google-genai. Store the key as GEMINI_API_KEY. Use it as a web AI fallback from Pi scripts.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'pip uninstall google-genai'. Delete ~/aiweb if unused. Remove GEMINI_API_KEY from .bashrc, .profile, .env, or systemd service files.

Name: Anthropic Claude API
Cost: Paid per token/model; pricing depends on selected Claude model and usage.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Create a Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv ~/aiweb && source ~/aiweb/bin/activate && pip install anthropic. Store the key as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Use it when you want stronger remote reasoning.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'pip uninstall anthropic'. Delete ~/aiweb if unused. Remove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .bashrc, .profile, .env, or systemd service files.

Name: Mistral AI API
Cost: Free/evaluation tier may be available; production use usually requires paid access.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Create a Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv ~/aiweb && source ~/aiweb/bin/activate && pip install mistralai. Store the key as MISTRAL_API_KEY. Use it as another web AI option.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'pip uninstall mistralai'. Delete ~/aiweb if unused. Remove MISTRAL_API_KEY from .bashrc, .profile, .env, or systemd service files.

Name: Groq API
Cost: Paid/on-demand API pricing; cost depends on model and usage.
How to install on a raspberry pi: Use the OpenAI-compatible API approach. Create a Python virtual environment, install the OpenAI client with 'pip install openai', set GROQ_API_KEY, and point the client at Groq's OpenAI-compatible base URL.
How to uninstall from a raspberry pi: Run 'pip uninstall openai' if only used for Groq. Delete ~/aiweb if unused. Remove GROQ_API_KEY from .bashrc, .profile, .env, or systemd service files.
